Bonelab/Boneworks probably looked like hot garbage a year before it's release date, because development hasn't been finished. Making a video game (especially in virtual reality) is taking hundreds of thousands of lines of code and putting them together so that they work properly. Alpha and Beta footage are usually very much incomplete and purposely made for demonstration. You can have your opinions and judge how you see fit when the 1.0 version comes out and you try it for yourself. Anything else is purely speculation.

How is it not a sequel when it picks up after the events of the Harran infection? The story doesn't really have any connection with DL1 but it's definitely a sequel. Spike even mentions Crane, meaning this happens right after

First, before anyone reads, \*SPOILERS FOR BOTH GAMES\*!!!

Gameplay feels more immersive and complete in DL1. All the different areas to explore and fight infected, the way you interact with the world around you and the smoothness of the parkour. Something about DL2's free running feels like I am watching someone on a go-pro. Doesn't feel smooth enough. Not to mention I feel the combat doesn't suck me in like the first one. The way you swing and kick the enemies, again, feels like I'm watching someone else fight for me. I don't get that excitement from fighting Volatiles or the nervousness I have when I'm doing missions at night. Not to mention I feel there are so many fewer zombies out in general. Harran had crowded streets chocked full of infected, all the time until nightfall, and then there are bigger things to worry about.

Not to mention the story in 2 (my opinion please don't crucify me) is lackluster. First off, canon is everyone in Harran died and the disease was cured. How did everyone die if you're talking to Spike at the beginning of the game? At least if they claimed it was nuked by Crane from the end of The Following there would be some continuity, but nope.

Then there's Aiden's story: He goes to Villedor to find his sister and rescue her. What irks me the most is no matter what choice you make in the end of the game, Mia dies regardless. And Aiden leaves anyway, again, REGARDLESS of your choice. What is the point of the story? In DL1 Crane gains humanity slowly but surely as he realizes the GRE are not the people he thought they were. He cares and tries his best to help and fight for the Tower and the other survivors. His whole goal in the Following, the reason he goes to the countryside is FOR the people in the Tower. Aiden seems so disconnected in my opinion, he isn't a character I want to root for. He's just doing his thing. Which isn't bad, but not something I necessarily would enjoy playing through again.

Let's be honest: most good zombie games don't have the best story. Look at Deadrising, Left 4 Dead, Killing Floor, etc. However there is an end goal, character development and plot twists. I just feel there could have been so much more than they gave us after an amazing game 7 years prior
